> **What you can defend when you leave.** Begin with a curiosity you own, then decide how you and your tools will work while nothing is yet at stake, so the rules exist when the pressure arrives.

## Start without a tool {#opening-move}

Research starts with something that will not leave you alone: a
pattern you keep noticing, a contradiction, a decision you want to
understand. Close every AI tool; this first move is yours. Write
four lines by hand.

1. One thing you genuinely want to understand, in one sentence.
2. Why an answer would matter, and to whom.
3. What you currently think the answer might be. A starting belief,
   not a claim.
4. One kind of evidence that could make you revise that belief.

No AI on this page: do not ask a tool to generate, improve, or rank
your curiosity. Keep what you wrote. Lesson 1 widens it into
candidate curiosities, and every rule this studio sets exists to
protect it.

## The milestone ahead {#checkpoint}

These first two studios run in four beats: your human curiosity, then your ledger and rules, then verified AI assistance, then a formal research question. This studio owns the first two beats and opens the third. Every studio after it asks you to delegate real work to AI and stand behind the result under your own name; the rules for that cannot be improvised under deadline pressure. This first milestone writes them down: what stays yours, what gets delegated, and how every delegation gets recorded and checked. Once the ledger exists, AI joins, and its first job may be a brainstorm that stretches your curiosity, under your rules. The rest of the book leans on this agreement, and your final defense in Studio 12 reads it back to you.

This studio closes with **[Milestone 1: Your working agreement](milestone01-govern-the-work.qmd)**, a short chapter of its own after the lessons. **What it asks you to produce.** A responsibility statement naming what you will never delegate, your AI and data-handling rules, your opened AI Research Ledger, and an early red-flag screen of your project idea.

Milestone 2 takes the curiosity that survived your red-flag screen, stretched by whatever brainstorming you licensed, and turns it into the arc's fourth beat: a formal question whose answer you could recognize. The milestone chapter keeps the working details: the practice steps, the versioned record, and how the artifact is assessed.

## The lessons in this studio

Read them in order, working each lesson's **It is your turn** as you go. Each one builds a piece of Milestone 1; beside each lesson is the piece it hands you.

- [Lesson 1 — AI Is Your Arm, Not Your Brain](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part1-research-with-ai/01-ai-is-your-arm-not-your-brain.html): your opened AI Research Ledger, three genuine curiosities, and one first AI exchange already logged and verified.
- [Lesson 2 — The Student as Research Director](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part1-research-with-ai/02-the-student-as-research-director.html): your delegation map: the road's tasks sorted into safe to delegate, delegate then verify, and never delegate.
- [Lesson 3 — Specify, Delegate, Interrogate, Inspect, Verify, Document, Defend](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part1-research-with-ai/03-specify-delegate-interrogate-inspect-verify-document-defend.html): one complete SDIIVDD run on a checkable claim, with the verification you ran and what it caught.
- [Lesson 4 — Research Responsibility and Intellectual Ownership](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part1-research-with-ai/04-research-responsibility-and-intellectual-ownership.html): your ownership statement, your never-delegate list, and a first draft of your AI-use disclosure.

When the last lesson closes, the milestone chapter is next. Nothing you write in a lesson is busywork: every piece above is on the milestone's checklist.
